articles.title: Howard Stern and wife Beth turned the loss of their dog Bianca into an animal-rescue legacy; a 14,000-square-foot cat adoption centre now operates in her name, and Beth has helped rehome over 2,000 cats since 2013
articles.summary: The death of a much-loved English bulldog in 2012 set radio host Howard Stern and his wife, Beth Stern, on a journey that would change animal rescue
articles.body: The death of a much-loved English bulldog in 2012 set radio host Howard Stern and his wife, Beth Stern, on a journey that would change animal rescue efforts across the United States. After their dog Bianca passed away, the couple turned their sadness into a nationwide fundraising campaign with North Shore Animal League America. Their efforts led to the creation of Bianca's Furry Friends Feline Adoption Center, a 14,000-square-foot facility on the second floor of the organisation's campus in Port Washington, New York. Since becoming directly involved with North Shore Animal League America as a volunteer foster parent in 2013, Beth Stern has personally cared for and helped find homes for more than 2,000 rescued cats and kittens, according to official records published by the organisation.Building a state-of-the-art rescue hubBianca's Furry Friends Feline Adoption Center opened after a major fundraising campaign led by the Stern family. The centre was designed to give shelter cats a better place to live while waiting to be adopted. According to North Shore Animal League America, the 14,000-square-foot facility has open, cage-free rooms where cats can move around freely instead of being kept in traditional metal cages. Large windows stretching from floor to ceiling let in natural sunlight. Special climbing walls, raised platforms, and small spaces for cats to hide and rest also help keep the animals active and comfortable. The new centre allowed North Shore Animal League America to double the number of cats it could rescue and care for on campus. Moving the cats to the new upper-floor facility also freed up a large amount of space on the ground floor of the main building. This allowed the organisation to take in more rescued dogs and puppies. The facility also has a separate medical room, a surgery room, a nursery for nursing mothers, and special isolation rooms for animals recovering from infectious diseases or operations.From personal grief to hands-on fosteringThe idea for the adoption centre came from the couple's close bond with their bulldog, Bianca, who was often mentioned on Howard Stern's radio show. After Bianca died, Beth Stern began focusing much of her public work on directly helping animals in need. As a spokesperson and volunteer foster parent for North Shore Animal League America, Beth uses the couple's home in New York as a temporary shelter for animals that need extra attention and medical care. "Fostering is the most rewarding thing I have ever done in my life," Beth Stern said in a profile published by North Shore Animal League America. "Taking in an animal that is sick, scared, or neglected, nursing them back to health, and then finding them a loving forever home is an incredible experience." Her fostering work mainly focuses on animals that are especially vulnerable. These include newborn orphaned kittens that need bottle feeding around the clock, pregnant cats, and animals suffering from physical injuries or serious medical conditions.Broadening public support and adoption eventsAlong with fostering animals and helping develop the adoption centre, the Sterns use public events to raise money and awareness for shelters that do not put healthy or treatable animals down. Beth Stern hosts major national animal welfare programmes, including the annual Kitten Bowl on the Great American Family channel. The event is organised in partnership with North Shore Animal League America and aims to encourage people across the country to adopt shelter animals. The attention brought by Bianca's Furry Friends has also helped increase adoption efforts across the region. North Shore Animal League America, which is recognised as the world's largest no-kill rescue and adoption organisation, reports that it has saved more than 1.1 million animal lives since it was founded in 1944. Howard Stern also regularly talks about the adoption centre's work on The Howard Stern Show on SiriusXM. He encourages listeners to consider adopting animals, volunteering at shelters, or becoming foster parents.Operational expansion and specialized careHaving a separate cat facility allows medical staff at North Shore Animal League America to provide special treatment for serious feline illnesses. These include upper respiratory infections and ringworm. Such conditions can sometimes lead traditional municipal shelters to euthanise affected animals. Bianca's Furry Friends has separate quarantine rooms where veterinary teams can treat sick cats without putting other animals in the shelter at risk of infection. The adoption centre also has special meeting rooms where people interested in adopting can spend time with cats in a comfortable, home-like setting before completing the adoption process. Beth Stern continues to take in groups of rescued kittens throughout the year. She regularly shares updates about their recovery and development on her social media accounts. These posts help introduce the animals to potential adopters and give them a better chance of finding permanent, loving homes.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: Twitch streamer Maxwell “Plaqueboymax” has questioned Adin Ross over his comments about Black culture after Ross suggested that he and his friends could wear blackface for a livestream. The discussion started after Ross watched a clip of Plaqueboymax and his friends dressed as white men during their Halloween livestream. Ross called their outfits hilarious and suggested doing something similar with a different racial look. Plaqueboymax later challenged the idea, asking why Ross did not show more respect for the culture that had played a major role in his success.Adin Ross suggests doing a blackface livestream with Cheesur and KonvyThe discussion began during Adin Ross' Kick livestream on October 31, 2026. He was watching a video from Plaqueboymax's Halloween broadcast, where the Twitch streamer and his friends appeared dressed as white men.Ross found their outfits funny and then brought up an idea of his own. He suggested that he, Nermin “Cheesur” and Steven “Konvy” could do a livestream wearing blackface. He even asked his viewers whether such a stream would receive criticism.Ross said:"Nah, bro, they're not talking ****. They're acting like white kids. This is hilarious. Hear me out - what if Max did a stream with everyone - boom. And then me, Cheesur, Konvy, but we all do blackface, bro? I ain't going to lie. That would be a banger stream, chat. I ain't going to lie, bro. Bro, that would be a banger stream, bro. I ain't going to lie, bro. What do you mean, 'GG'? If they could do it, I could do it. I'm Jewish; I'm not white. That's first of all. Bro, chat, be honest, bro - do you guys think I would get hate for doing that, though?"Ross also tried to explain his thinking by saying that he was Jewish and not white. However, he still wanted to know whether viewers would criticize him for wearing blackface.Plaqueboymax did not seem to agree with the idea. His response went beyond the Halloween outfits and focused on Ross' relationship with Black culture.Plaqueboymax questions Adin Ross' respect for Black culture and calls him a streaming GOATDuring his livestream on November 1, Plaqueboymax addressed Ross' remarks and explained why they bothered him. He said that a large part of Ross' success came from Black culture and questioned why the Kick streamer did not show it enough respect.Plaqueboymax said:"A lot of your success is rooted in Black culture. Like, a lot of it! So, my question is... why don't you respect Black culture? Like, literally. I feel like if you had the respect of Black culture, if that was there, a lot of the **** that went on in these past couple of years that you didn't **** with, would not have happened. On god. Who else is going to say this besides Plaqueboy?"He was not simply questioning Ross' Halloween idea. Plaqueboymax suggested that the streamer needed to think about how his comments could affect the culture that had helped him build his career.There was also a personal side to his reaction. articles.summary: Mexican television presenter Ines Gomez Mont, who once made headlines for asking NFL legend Tom Brady to marry her, has been arrested in Miami after
articles.body: Mexican television presenter Ines Gomez Mont, who once made headlines for asking NFL legend Tom Brady to marry her, has been arrested in Miami after spending nearly five years outside Mexico amid a massive fraud investigation. The 43-year-old was detained by US authorities on October 30, 2026, in connection with allegations of organised crime, money laundering and tax fraud.According to Mexican news agency reports and Mexico's Attorney General's Office (FGR), Gomez Mont is accused of being part of an alleged criminal network that siphoned public money through a series of bogus companies and fraudulent invoices. Her lawyer husband, Victor Manuel Alvarez Puga, is also accused of being involved in the operation, which investigators estimate involved around 2.95 billion pesos, or approximately £120 million.The former television host was reportedly taken into custody in Miami, Florida, where she was photographed being escorted by police officers in handcuffs. She is currently in US custody, pending immigration proceedings and any formal extradition process to Mexico.Ines Gomez Mont and husband fled Mexico in 2021Gomez Mont and Alvarez Puga left Mexico with their family in September 2021 after arrest warrants were issued against them over the alleged financial scam. The couple had remained outside the country as Mexican authorities continued their investigation.Their arrest comes weeks after Interpol reportedly withdrew the international red notices against the pair in September 2026. Despite the removal of the notices, the arrest warrants issued in Mexico remained active.Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum had criticised Interpol's decision and maintained that her government would continue seeking the couple's extradition. Mexican prosecutors said the presenter's arrest followed an exchange of information between Mexican and US authorities.According to reports, Mexican investigators had located the couple in Miami as early as 2022. However, a formal extradition request was not made until December 2025.What are the allegations against the TV presenter?Investigators allege that the couple were connected to a network of companies that issued fraudulent invoices and created contracts for services that were never actually delivered. The money was allegedly routed through multiple bank transactions to conceal its origin.The alleged operation is said to have involved funds from Mexico's Ministry of the Interior during the presidency of Enrique Pena Nieto. At least 18 million pesos reportedly ended up in bank accounts belonging to Gomez Mont and her husband.Alvarez Puga, who has been dubbed the 'King of the Invoice Mills', is accused of masterminding the alleged operation. Investigators have also linked him to a network of contacts involving politicians, former government officials, lawyers, businesspeople and celebrities.The lawyer was reportedly detained by US immigration officers in Miami in 2025 over irregularities concerning his stay in the country. He was subsequently released, and his current whereabouts remain unclear.President Sheinbaum has previously accused the couple of being involved in fraudulent invoicing. She has also called for cooperation from Washington, pointing to Mexico's transfer of around 100 prisoners wanted by the Trump administration to the United States.Ines Gomez Mont has maintained her innocenceGomez Mont has denied the allegations since the case came to light. In October 2021, shortly after the warrants were issued, she addressed the controversy in a statement shared with her 2.5 million Instagram followers.She said she had faith that the truth would emerge and that her innocence would be established. Calling the allegations an injustice, she insisted that she would continue to speak out despite what she described as attempts to silence her.The presenter has not been convicted of the alleged offences. The allegations against her and her husband remain subject to legal proceedings.Ines Gomez Mont once asked Tom Brady to marry herApart from her television career and the ongoing fraud case, Gomez Mont was also known internationally for an unusual moment involving former NFL quarterback Tom Brady.During the 2008 Super Bowl, while reporting on the event, she famously asked Brady to marry her. The football star turned down the proposal, making the exchange a memorable moment from her time covering the sporting event.Years later, the presenter has again made international headlines, this time following her arrest in the United States over the allegations linked to the multi-million-pound fraud investigation.You use AI every day. articles.title: Now kids want to know why they are learning something, says Inventure Academy’s Nooraine Fazal
articles.summary: Nooraine Fazal of Inventure Academy on Bengaluru’s change, kids’ learning shift to “why,” experiential education, less sport, and giving children freedom.
articles.body: Best Of Ooru | Nooraine Fazal is founder, CEO and managing trustee of Bengaluru-based school chain Inventure Academy, established in 2005. An educationist, entrepreneur and former Karnataka women’s cricket and basketball player, she holds an MS in Management from Boston UniversityYou’ve lived and worked in several cities abroad. What did you miss most about Bengaluru—and what surprised you when you returned?What I missed most about Bengaluru varied depending on when and where I lived. When I was in London (1991–93), it was just about everything, starting with people and food! It took me a while to come to terms with the fact that I had chosen to leave India to learn more about the world, and myself.While living in the desert sands of Dubai and Abu Dhabi, it was Bengaluru’s greenery and weather that I missed most.What surprised me most when I returned was how much Bengaluru had transformed. It had been my small, friendly city, where I couldn’t move an inch without my parents somehow finding out where I was (this was pre-mobile era!). I returned to a larger, bustling IT city that was home to people from across India, and increasingly, expats.As much as I loved Bengaluru’s new energy and diversity, I was disheartened to see a city racing ahead in growth while falling behind in livability — its lakes and greenery giving way to concrete and glass structures, and its public infrastructure struggling to keep pace.You represented Karnataka in cricket and basketball. Which Bengaluru grounds and courts shaped you?My sporting journey began on the fields of Clarence High School—one on campus, the other 2–3 km away on Assaye Road. Getting to the latter was an adventure in itself! We walked or cycled, crossed railway tracks on foot, and then cleaned the field before marking it for Sports Day. Can’t imagine middle- or upper-middle-class school kids being required by the school to do that today—would probably make for a viral post or two on social media!It was on those fields that I discovered my potential as a sportsperson. I had just joined Clarence and very quickly found myself selected as the school hockey goalkeeper. All of 11 years old (and pretty short then!), I was keeping goal for the senior school team, with cricket pads, fast reflexes and lots of courage (or was that stupidity?!) as my armour.And then, of course, came Mount Carmel (which I absolutely loved for the sports and leadership opportunities), KSCA, IISc, Kanteerava, MICO, and the courts at Malleswaram and Jayanagar.Sport took me across Bengaluru and India—and, thankfully, out of the classroom, where we were generally expected to sit quietly, take notes and memorise them for the year-end exam!Where do you go when you want an unhurried afternoon in the city?Nandi Hills! It was my favourite getaway growing up. I cycled there as a pre-teen and graduated to a motorcycle as a teenager (err, yes, I may have been underage!). And it remains a favourite to this day.Which Bengaluru dish would you happily cross the city for?Mom’s Kutchi Biryani — by far the best in the world! (And anyone who has tasted it will vouch for that!) No restaurant in Bengaluru comes close. And I do cross from the Republic of Whitefield to head to my parents home in Fraser Town regularly for it!From Gen Z to Gen Alpha, what changes do you see in the way Bengaluru’s children think and learn?Children increasingly want to know why they’re learning something. What’s the relevance? Why memorise what they can look up in seconds?There’s a greater appetite for hands-on, experiential and project-based learning, and for exploring interests beyond academics, particularly the arts. They’re also spending far more time online—learning, creating, connecting and, yes, playing video games!At the same time, they’re increasingly competitive, with getting admission into a great college seen as the pathway to success. Their lives are packed with tuitions, activity classes and organised schedules, leaving little time for spontaneous play and informal learning.What worries me is that children have fewer opportunities to navigate friendships, disagreements and failures without adult intervention. That’s where so much social-emotional learning happens!As a former sportsperson, I also worry that children play far less sport. There’s perhaps more interest in being fit, and looking fit, but that’s very different from playing on a team, learning to win and lose, working hard together, and simply having fun.Of course, neither generation is homogeneous. These shifts also reflect the environments we, as parents, educators and society, have created.Less memorisation, more questioning and learning by doing is welcome. But at what cost to independence and learning from life beyond the classroom?Is there a message on early learning that you’d like to share with young parents?Let your children be children!Give them the freedom to explore, experiment and mess up sometimes, with a safety net and sensible guardrails, rather than trying to protect them from every disappointment or difficulty.Some of my biggest learnings came from the streets and playing fields of Bengaluru. From dealing with bullying, a teacher who simply didn’t believe in me (more than compensated for by those who did—so yes, you win some, you lose some!), friendships and heartbreaks, success and failure, and even discord at home.These experiences taught me to shut out the noise, find my own voice and recognise that life isn’t always black and white. It’s often about finding the right shade of grey, learning to understand and respect different perspectives and ways of being, without necessarily agreeing with them, and recognising that there are many pathways to success.Children need love, trust and guidance, but also the space to figure things out for themselves. We can’t live their lives for them, nor should we try to.After all, isn’t growing up about so much more than learning to read, write and count? It’s about learning to navigate life!You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: SC orders trial in Ram temple donation case; SIT says Rs 2.7 crore stolen
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Five months after news broke of pilferage of donations at Ayodhya Ram temple, Supreme Court cleared trial of eight people, who figure in the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Five months after news broke of pilferage of donations at Ayodhya Ram temple, Supreme Court cleared trial of eight people, who figure in the chargesheet filed by the SIT for allegedly siphoning Rs 2.7 crore. It also gave the petitioners, who had sought probe, the status of victims of crime and allowed them to assist in the trial, reports Dhananjay Mahapatra.The SIT's status report informed SC that financial and forensic examination extended to cash deposits, transactions, property purchases, construction expenditure, vehicles, jewellery, other assets, and event-related spendings. "The amount of alleged embezzlement is approximately Rs 2.7 crore," the report said.On Monday, solicitor general Tushar Mehta explained to the court the process that involved scrutiny of bank accounts and acquisition of immoveable properties by the accused, as well as examination of CCTV footage that culminated in the chargesheet Sept 23.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the trial court to proceed with the trial in accordance with law. On the large number of petitioners who had sought an independent probe into the donation theft, the bench said the petitioners can be given the status of victims of crime, and in public interest, they can assist the prosecutor and trial court in proceedings.One of the petitioners also sought a direction from SC for an “independent, impartial, technically competent survey/demarcation” of the land that was allotted for the temple by SC in its Nov 9, 2019, judgement.He also sought a direction to the revenue and statutory authorities to place before SC relevant records and their comparison with the site plan and actual location of the Ram Janmabhoomi Temple complex to determine if the present complex stands on the land allotted by the court.While Mehta said it is impermissible for the petitioner to seek a virtual reopening of the judgement by a fivejudge bench, the bench said if the petitioner had any grievance about the demarcation of the land, he should approach the civil court with a civil suit.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Paris Hilton launched a recovery fund for women-owned businesses after disasters; a year after her Los Angeles wildfire grants, 90% of recipient businesses were still operating
articles.summary: When natural disasters destroy homes and neighbourhoods, small businesses can face a difficult recovery of their own.
articles.body: When natural disasters destroy homes and neighbourhoods, small businesses can face a difficult recovery of their own. For women who depend on those businesses to support their families, losing a workplace can also mean losing a source of income and the livelihoods of employees. Paris Hilton has launched a new initiative aimed at helping women business owners facing that situation across the US. As reported by The Associated Press, the Back in Business Recovery Fund follows a programme she supported after the 2025 Los Angeles wildfires, when grants helped dozens of businesses deal with the immediate costs of rebuilding.Paris Hilton commits $350,000 to new recovery fundHilton has pledged $350,000 to establish the Back in Business Recovery Fund, which aims to raise at least $1 million by the end of March. The initiative is being run through her social impact organisation, 11:11 Media Impact, in partnership with GoFundMe.org, the charitable arm of the fundraising platform. GoFundMe.org is contributing a further $100,000 towards the launch, according to The Associated Press reports.The programme is intended to reach women who own small businesses affected by disasters across the country. Rather than being limited to one type of emergency or a particular industry, it is designed to provide financial assistance when businesses are struggling to reopen or maintain operations after a damaging event.Hilton said her involvement came partly from seeing how much locally owned businesses contribute to the communities around them. She also wanted to extend the work beyond Los Angeles, where she had previously helped provide financial support to business owners affected by the fires.Paris Hilton's earlier wildfire fund helped businesses cover rent, wages and rebuilding costsThe new fund builds on a programme Hilton backed following the January 2025 wildfires in Los Angeles. The fires destroyed her Malibu home, where she had been raising her young children, and left many other residents facing the loss of their properties and livelihoods.In the aftermath, Hilton's organisation and GoFundMe.org distributed more than $1 million in grants to 50 women-owned small businesses. Individual awards reached up to $25,000, with recipients using the money for expenses including rent, staff wages, replacement equipment and rebuilding damaged premises.Among those helped were owners of childcare centres, bakeries, bookshops, dance studios and beauty salons. Many of the businesses had been affected by the Eaton fire, which caused extensive destruction in Altadena.For Hilton, the experience of losing her own home brought the financial difficulties facing other mothers into sharper focus. Renata Ortega told The Associated Press, “Nothing prepares you for that amount of loss.”90% of Los Angeles grant recipients were still operating a year laterA year after the grants were distributed, 90% of the recipient businesses remained in operation, according to the Pasadena Women's Business Center reported by The Associated Press. The organisation also received funding to offer technical support and mentoring to businesses affected by the fires.For some owners, the grants helped meet costs that might otherwise have prevented them from reopening, while others were able to replace equipment or secure premises from which to continue trading. Renata Ortega, owner of Orla Floral Studio, was among the recipients. She had operated her floral design business from a converted garage beside her home in Altadena, where she lived with her husband and three dogs. The Eaton fire destroyed the property, including her studio and the equipment she had accumulated over several years.The loss left her uncertain about whether she could continue the business. She was also concerned about the people whose income depended on her work, including her employees and flower market suppliers.The grant helped Ortega put down a deposit on a new studio and buy a replacement floral cooler. Those purchases allowed her to resume operations without losing her existing staff. She said the business had since become busy again and that she was considering taking on another employee.Hilton continued supporting businesses after the grantsHilton's involvement with some of the Los Angeles recipients extended beyond the initial financial assistance. Reportedly, she became a customer of several businesses, wearing a catsuit from clothing retailer Crop It Like It's Hot at the Coachella music festival and bringing local food vendors, including Carmela Ice Cream and Hot Shrimp Mami, to her events.Hilton, the great-granddaughter of hotel magnate Conrad N. Hilton, also spoke about being underestimated during her career. She said she had worked to establish herself as more than the public image many people associated with her.According to Wells Fargo figures cited in the announcement, the US has 14.5 million women-owned businesses, representing 39% of all businesses. Yet women, particularly those from minority communities, continue to receive a smaller share of venture capital and loan funding than men.Rebecca Grone, director of 11:11 Media Impact, said women business owners often have fewer financial resources available to them. Those with primary responsibility for caring for children or other family members can also face additional pressures when trying to recover after a disaster.Women's business centres will help identify grant recipientsThe Back in Business Recovery Fund will work with some of the approximately 150 women's business centres operating across the US. These organisations are expected to help identify business owners affected by disasters and connect them with financial assistance.The grants will be unrestricted, allowing recipients to decide how best to use the money for their businesses. The approach follows the Los Angeles programme, where owners were able to direct funding towards immediate operating costs, equipment and other needs.Amanda Brown Lierman, executive director of GoFundMe.org, said, “Collaborating with the centers will help identify impacted women quickly and opens up access not just to cash, but to a community of business owners facing similar challenges.”The timing of the fund's activation will depend partly on assessments from these centres. They will help establish where assistance is needed and when the programme should respond.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Prince William apologises after backlash over 3,000-acre Bradninch Estate sale; tenants demand fair valuations, King Charles disappointed as Duchy of Cornwall faces capital gains tax questions
articles.summary: Prince William has reportedly apologised to tenants of the Bradninch Estate in Devon following a backlash over his decision to sell the 3,000-acre
articles.body: Prince William has reportedly apologised to tenants of the Bradninch Estate in Devon following a backlash over his decision to sell the 3,000-acre property, which forms part of the Duchy of Cornwall. The Prince of Wales is said to have been unhappy with reports highlighting residents' concerns about the proposed sale, with some tenants fearing they could lose their homes and livelihoods.According to a report by The Observer, William contacted the Duchy's rural director, Matthew Morris, last Sunday to discuss the growing controversy. Morris subsequently visited the estate on Thursday and met with tenants to address their concerns.During the meeting, the royal representative reportedly apologised for underestimating the time required to complete the land disposal process. He also agreed to arrange fresh independent valuations of the farms and residential properties, with the assessments to be jointly commissioned by the tenants and the Duchy.One tenant described Morris as being "all apologetic", while another reportedly welcomed the conciliatory approach but cautioned that "the proof will be in the pudding".Why Prince William's property sale has sparked backlashThe apology follows growing concerns among residents after the Duchy began the process of selling the Bradninch Estate, a 1,215-hectare (3,000-acre) property in Devon. The estate has been part of the Duchy of Cornwall since the 14th century and represents approximately one-fifth of the land portfolio William inherited from his father, King Charles III, in September 2022.The decision to sell the estate is part of William's wider plan to concentrate future Duchy investment on five geographical heartlands: the Isles of Scilly, Cornwall, Dartmoor, Bath and Kennington in south London.However, the proposed sale has caused considerable anxiety among farming and residential tenants. Last month, possession orders reportedly gave some residents just six months to either purchase their properties or leave.While tenants have been offered the opportunity to buy their homes and farms, some say the valuations are too high and do not adequately account for the money they have invested in improving the properties over the years. Others have raised concerns about their ability to afford the purchases.The controversy has also drawn criticism from Mary Ryan, a former GP who has lived in Bradninch for 36 years and is supporting affected tenants. She has accused William of hypocrisy, arguing that his commitment to tackling homelessness and mental health issues could come at the expense of rural families facing uncertainty over their own homes.Kensington Palace responds to tenants' concernsFollowing the backlash, a Kensington Palace spokesperson told The Observer that the concerns surrounding the sale were being taken seriously and that tenants were receiving individual support."We recognise that these are important and deeply personal decisions. Every tenant is being supported through the process on an individual basis, with access to practical guidance from the estate team, independent welfare and mental health support services and ongoing discussions about what is right for their circumstances," the spokesperson said.The statement also explained that the sale was part of a long-term strategy to direct future Duchy of Cornwall investment towards areas where it could deliver greater benefits for communities, farming, nature and the local economy."We will continue to support tenants with care, respect and fairness, whatever decision they ultimately make," the spokesperson added.The Duchy has also said that tenants are being offered the first opportunity to purchase their homes and farms, with discounts taking into account factors such as the length of their tenancy, the type of agreement and investments made in the properties.According to the Duchy, eight out of nine farming tenants are actively exploring the purchase of some or all of their farms, while around two-thirds of residential tenants are considering buying their homes.Questions raised over tax implications of the saleThe proposed disposal has also prompted questions about whether the Duke of Cornwall should pay capital gains tax on the proceeds.A Duchy spokesperson has maintained that the Duke is exempt because proceeds from the disposal of capital assets are required by law to be reinvested and are not available for his personal use.However, tax expert Dan Neidle has challenged that interpretation, arguing that there is no legal basis for such an exemption. He has suggested that if HM Revenue and Customs determines that capital gains tax is payable, the Duke would be required to pay it.The controversy has also reportedly disappointed King Charles, who regularly visited the Bradninch Estate when he was Prince of Wales and regarded it as an example of the rural communities that form the backbone of Britain.For now, the promise of fresh independent valuations has offered some reassurance to tenants. However, residents are still waiting to see whether the Duchy's revised approach will address their concerns over affordability, property improvements and their future on the estate.You use AI every day. articles.title: Investment in renewable energy cushioned Iran war blow: PM Modi
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi said India's economic growth has remained high despite the West Asia crisis, whose impact would have been far more serious if
articles.body: NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi said India's economic growth has remained high despite the West Asia crisis, whose impact would have been far more serious if the country had not invested in clean energy over the past decade.Commending India's progress in renewable energy sector, he said efforts were on to add 500GW of non-fossil energy capacity over the next 10-11 years. The PM also pitched for a "clean cooking movement" to reduce dependence on imported gas.Speaking at the inauguration of Bharat Renewable Energy Summit at Bharat Mandapam Monday, Modi said the ongoing energy crisis had underlined the link between energy security and economic security, making it imperative for countries to reduce dependence on fossil fuels."This global crisis has given every country a clear message that energy security is directly linked to economic security. If we continue to remain too dependent on fossil fuels, global economy will continue to be disrupted again and again," he said.Modi said India had already achieved nearly 300GW of non-fossil installed power capacity, accounting for more than 50% of its total capacity, and was pursuing its target of 500GW capacity by 2030.India's clean energy sector could offer investment opportunities exceeding Rs 20 lakh crore ($220 billion) by the end of the decade as the country expands renewable energy generation, transmission infrastructure, manufacturing and energy storage. More than Rs 15 lakh crore ($164 billion) had been invested in the sector over the past decade, including Rs 6 lakh crore ($63 billion) in the last two years."For all of you, a new sky of opportunities is about to open up in India's clean energy sector," he said, adding it was difficult to find "political and policy stability" like India's anywhere in the world.Referring to schemes such as PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana and PM-Kusum, Modi said India was making solar power part of citizens' lives. He called on farmers to move beyond solar pumps and become energy producers by installing panels on vacant farmland and along field boundaries. "Annadata should become Urjadata," he said.In a push to reduce dependence on imported cooking gas, Modi urged startups and innovators to develop solutions that would enable households to use rooftop solar power for cooking. He also pitched for wider adoption of electric vehicles, with households charging them using solar power generated on their rooftops.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
